newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen quiet before Telekom float.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen quiet before Telekom float.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to hover in a narrow band this week in weak volumes, ahead of the flotation of shares in telephone giant Deutsch Telekom next Monday, traders said.
But other dealers said on Monday that the market could build on record highs reached last week and attempt to breach the 2,750 point level for the DAX index.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day electronic dealings in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, was down 4.43 points, or 0.16 percent, at 2,727.86, as the dollar dipped below 1.50 marks for the first time since the beginning of September.
"The level of the dollar is an irritation for us," said one trader.
Dealers saw support coming from a firm start on Wall Street, but said volumes in the U.S. were thin with some players away because of the Veterans' Day holiday.
The Deutsche Telekom flotation, set to be the largest in Europe's history, will cause busy trade next week on the Frankfurt bourse, which will extend its hours especially.
Traders said they expected the DAX index to make further strides after the Telekom sale, and said it could add another 100 points before the year-end to reach 2,850 points.

Schering shares performed well, climbing 55 pfennigs to 125.40 marks, after the firm announced positive nine-month figures and traders said a major investment house had upgraded its recommendation on the stock.
Fresenius Medical Care also moved ahead, touching a year high of 148.95 marks, and then traded up 9.40 marks, or almost seven percent, at 145.90 marks.
Dealers said the stock was reacting belatedly to nine month results released on Friday, which were better than first appeared, and also ahead of the issue of preference shares later in the month.
